info.name: FreeDailyPro Public APIs
info.description:
REST + MCP APIs for FreeDailyPro's tools -- text, PDF, security, calculators, SEO/design, business documents, and planning. One API key, one shared usage pool across every category and both MCP endpoints.

Before you start: set the fdp_api_key variable in the FreeDailyPro environment (top right environment selector) to your own key from https://www.freedailypro.com/developers -- free tier is 20,000 calls/month, no credit card required. Billing, usage, and plan upgrades are all handled on freedailypro.com, not through Postman.

Run "Get Started" > "Health check" first (no key needed), then "Word count" to confirm your key and environment are wired up.

item.name: PDF & Document Tools
Parse a PDF's fillable form fields

request.description: multipart/form-data. Attach a PDF with real AcroForm fields under the 'file' key.
multipart/form-data. 'values' is a JSON string mapping field names to the values to fill in. Returns the filled PDF as binary.

item.name: Permanently redact areas of a PDF

request.description: multipart/form-data. 'boxes' maps page index -> array of {x,y,w,h} boxes in fractional page coordinates (0-1). Redaction is permanent -- content underneath is removed, not just covered.

item.description: Base URL: pdf_base (the main freedailypro.com domain, not the utility API). All three take a PDF file as multipart/form-data.

item.name: MCP (Claude Desktop, Cursor, AI agents)

request.description: Same 3 PDF operations as the REST API, exposed as MCP tools for Claude Desktop, Cursor, and similar agents.
MCP takes file content as base64 in the request body, not multipart -- the difference from the REST version above.
All 127 utility-api endpoints (text, security, calculators, SEO/design, business, planning) exposed as MCP tools.
Same shared quota as every REST call above -- MCP and REST calls count against the same key, same limit.

item.description: Both endpoints use JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP. pdf_mcp covers PDF operations; utility_mcp covers everything else. Same X-API-Key, same shared quota as the REST folders above -- an MCP call and a REST call cost exactly the same.
